rows.evidence: Line 92 is the mismatch return of actorRefEquals, called only from replayInstall (:253) and replayActivate (:289). The install event is written with actor: command.identity.actor (role-memory-service.ts:367; activate :486), and the replay lookup is keyed by roleInstallIdentityKey/roleActivateIdentityKey (:133, :136), which fold commandIdentityKey (contracts/command-event.ts:98-106) and therefore the actor; sqlite lookupCommit matches that exact key plus fingerprint (sqlite-record-store.ts:507-540). A receipt found under the key can only be the commit of a command with the same actor, so a differing event actor needs an edited event (the deleted test wrapped eventAt: before R3g-role-spec.test.ts:531-546; T1-028). Caveat, not a refutation: install/activate are still unwired (production-reach allowlist 'RoleConfigurationPort.installRoleSpec' kept-for; create-platform.ts:1284-1288), so no route reaches them today either; keep for decision 6/34.
rows.proposal_note: Keeping it untested is right; deleting the redundant actor check is also safe (the identity key already folds the actor), but do not delete install/activate, which decision 6/34 reserves. No tamper test (rule 4).

rows.evidence: Line 310 arm 1 (since undefined) needs a stored round whose top-level since is absent. Both writers of VerificationRound records (grep: only evidence-service.ts:357 and :1700) create with {since:null} plus a commitCursorBinding on since (:352-358; :1700-1702) and updates copy the stored origin (:347-351); decodeNoticeOrigin refuses a persisted null (:394) and omits since only when the key is absent (:395-396). A since-less round is therefore pre-S5 data; the deleted test made it with legacyNoticeWire (before S5-queue-support.ts:287-296), which TP-063 removed.
rows.proposal_note: Deletion fits 79-1 ('代码只读当前格式 ... 不留旧版本的解码分支'). TP-157 leaves the 2B-24 legacy sentence to the lead and TP-063 already removed the legacy notice positions, so no current spec reserves this branch. Copying since unconditionally is behaviour-identical for the missing case; treating it as damaged is the stricter 79-1 reading. Add no test.

rows.evidence: The no-pin arm at :625 is taken when chainRefusal gets a non-busy refusal or a chain that is not 'head'. Its callers: :1105 and :1139 pass a roundOpenChainProblem result, which is busy with a head pin for kind 'head', null for 'none', and incomplete with no pin only for kind 'invalid' (verification-machine.ts:1220-1229); :1117 passes transitionRound(round_opened), but that call re-runs only values already checked at :1049-1105 (roundOpenProblem, verification-machine.ts:1114-1121) and prepareRoundOpening already ran roundOpenChecksProblem (:958), so decided.ok is true and :1117 never refuses. An invalid chain needs a foreign or old shape: root opens claim the subject slot (verification-machine.ts:1563-1564) and successors move it (:1538-1540); the deleted case was a slot-less legacy second root (before A2-verification-chain.test.ts:170-199).
rows.proposal_note: Keep it, no test; the live callers are :1105/:1139. Claude's ':1117 is effectively dead' is correct (my check agrees); removing that dead call would be a separate cleanup, not this U row.

rows.evidence: Switch arm 'invalid' at :1200 returns incomplete for a chain roundChainHead cannot judge. roundChainHead's invalid cases (verification-machine.ts:477-518: mixed subjects, two roots, duplicate or missing ordinal, wrong predecessor link, predecessor not finalized non-PASS) cannot be produced by current owners: a root claims the subject slot (verification-machine.ts:1563-1564), a successor must follow a finalized non-PASS head and moves the same slot (:1538-1540; buildSuccessorRound :629-673), and rounds are immutable. The deleted case seeded a slot-less second root (before A2-verification-chain.test.ts:170-199).
rows.proposal_note: Keep it, no test. Claude's 'pure invalid-chain cases belong in tests/state/verification-machine.test.ts' would unit-test roundChainHead with hand-built arrays; that is optional, not a restore of the deleted store-level tamper test, and rule 4 does not require it.

rows.evidence: Line 953 is the arrow that builds the reason for a compile rejection whose code is not 'invalid' (:950-953). compileVerificationPlan returns only pin_mismatch (verification-plan.ts:64-66), missing_pin (:68-70) or invalid (:71-74, :83-84, :127); unknown_check/no_check_coverage are declared (:25-30) but never produced. At the only two call sites (:1107, :1994) the plan is read by the very planRef passed to compile (evidence-service.ts:1055-1058, :1867-1872), the record codec forces plan.ref to be the outer key and goalRef into the same project (plan-record-codecs.ts:848-850, :865-866), and the subject is proven active in that plan before prepareRoundOpening (:1062-1065; reverifyAdmissionProblem verification-machine.ts:1435-1437), so pin_mismatch and missing_pin cannot occur; only 'invalid' can, and that runs the :952 callback. The :953 arrow is dead.
rows.proposal_note: Delete only the non-invalid branch / make it always invalid(...). Keep the if and the invalid mapping: an explicit-intent-only adopted plan may have no required obligation (plan-validation.ts:65-82 skips the legacy obligation rule), so 'invalid' may still be reachable; keeping that mapping is harmless either way. Do not narrow the compiler's own result type while its boundary checks still return pin_mismatch/missing_pin; dropping the unused unknown_check/no_check_coverage is fine. The neighbouring :952 row C4-043 is a different question (the invalid path is reachable, so that arrow is a test gap, not D2).
